title: Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance
abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms can be viewed as feedback devices that compare a proposed move with the target distribution and then accept or reject it. In this paper the Maxwell demon is identified with the acceptance module: it measures a proposed edge, stores the outcome in the accept/reject bit, and uses that bit to shape the probability current. The decision bit carries a genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, whereas only its directional part is converted into a cooling information flow. The relative-entropy relaxation rate obeys $v(t)=\dot{\mathcal I}_{\rm cool}(t)+\dot S(t)$, which separates useful cooling from housekeeping circulation in nonreversible chains.
summary: This paper reinterprets MCMC sampling by modeling the acceptance step as a Maxwell's Demon, quantifying the flow of information. It derives an entropy balance equation that separates useful 'cooling' information from 'housekeeping' circulation. The work provides powerful diagnostics to analyze and accelerate sampling algorithms beyond simple relaxation time measurements.
main_problem: The paper aims to mathematically formalize the analogy between Maxwell's Demon and the acceptance module in Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms, linking it to information thermodynamics principles.
main_result: It establishes the information balance equation $v(t) = \dot{I}_{cool}(t) + \dot{S}(t)$, showing that acceleration requires maximizing the conversion of decision information into cooling current while minimizing housekeeping circulation.
method: The analysis uses information-theoretic tools, defining mutual information, cooling information flow, and entropy production rates within the framework of MCMC dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is the MCMC sampling process, viewed as a feedback device operating on a state space governed by a master equation. The analysis compares different MCMC kernels (local MH, learned proposal, irreversible drive) on a 50-state rugged ring.
key_observables: Decision Mutual Information ($M_{dec}$), Cooling Information Flow ($\dot{I}_{cool}$), Housekeeping Entropy Production ($\sigma_{hk}$), and the relative-entropy relaxation rate ($v(t)$).
important_parameters: The target distribution ($\pi(x)$), the acceptance/rejection mechanism, and the relaxation time ($	au_{1/2}$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on viewing the MCMC process through the lens of information flow, particularly distinguishing between useful cooling information and housekeeping circulation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually summarizes the Maxwell-demon interpretation, detailing the flow from Proposal to Measurement to Memory and Feedback to the probability current.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the Maxwell demon analogy in MCMC, deriving the core information balance equation, and then applying this framework to analyze and compare different MCMC kernels (local MH vs. learned/irreversible drives) using quantitative diagnostics.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of information thermodynamics to MCMC provides novel diagnostics for sampling efficiency, which has parallels in understanding energy dissipation and information flow in complex physical systems.
